criteria.text: Is the agent's stated reasoning consistent with the edits it actually made and the feedback it received (no post-hoc rationalization, no lucky guess)?
Did each refinement stage (lint, test) do real, feedback-responsive work toward the solution rather than cosmetic or no-op changes?
Maybe's map/bind do NOT wrap the user function in a blanket try/except that converts raised exceptions into Nothing; exceptions raised inside mapped/bound functions propagate.

For Either/Maybe, mapping/binding over a failure context (Left/Nothing) returns the failure unchanged without invoking the function, and amap short-circuits on a failure in either the function position or the value position.
`insert` lifts a bare value into the success/neutral configuration (e.g. Either.insert yields a Right, Maybe.insert yields a Just) with correct metadata, so identity laws hold.
IO's map/bind/amap build deferred computations so that no impure work runs until run() is invoked (side effects observed only at run time).
Extraction/branch methods are implemented from the stored data: either/maybe/option dispatch correctly on branch, and is_left/is_right/is_just/is_nothing report the actual context.
